question.text: The rate constant, the activation energy and the Arrhenius parameter of a chemical reaction at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow> <mn>25°C</mn></mrow> </math> are <math><mn>3.0</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math><mn>104.4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">kJ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>14</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. The value of the rate constant as <math><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></math> is

solution.text:
k=Ae-Ea/RT (Arrhenius equation)
when T→∞
k=Ae0 , or k=A
